speaker: Doctor

The CBC shows mild leukocytosis with neutrophilia, suggesting an inflammatory process, while the CRP is normal. Have you experienced any fevers, night sweats, or changes in bowel habits like urgency or tenesmus? Additionally, have you traveled recently or consumed any specific foods that might trigger these symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture
REQUEST TEST: Calprotectin

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Stool_Culture - NORMAL READINGS (Not provided in the data), Calprotectin - NORMAL READINGS (Not provided in the data).

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative stool culture and normal calprotectin make an acute infectious or severe inflammatory bowel disease less likely. Have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool, and does the pain improve after you have a bowel movement? Also, do you have a family history of colon cancer or inflammatory bowel disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Mucus (IBS-M). The clinical presentation of chronic diarrhea, relief of pain after defecation, urgency, and mucus, combined with normal inflammatory markers and negative stool culture, strongly supports this diagnosis despite the camping history which has likely been a red herring.
